source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Order the same fixed laboratory panel for every client regardless of procedure or health status","B":"Delay scheduling by obtaining routine tests even when results cannot influence perioperative care","C":"Replace the preoperative history and examination with a standardized set of laboratory results","D":"Select tests according to clinical history, comorbidities, procedure, and likely management impact"}}
source_row.rationale: Preoperative laboratory testing (individualized based on the client's health status, planned procedure, and risk factors, rather than a blanket approach for all clients) is intended to identify any underlying conditions or abnormalities (such as anemia, electrolyte imbalances, or coagulation issues) that could affect surgical or anesthesia risk, allowing the care team to optimize the client's condition or take appropriate precautions before proceeding.
source_row.source_detail: Preoperative testing is selected according to patient condition, procedure, and clinical indication rather than a universal panel; reviewed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: American Society of Anesthesiologists — Preoperative Evaluation Guidelines
